# At a glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Format | Standard (Reality Fracture, set code `fra`, plus Standard support) |
| Colors | Blue, black, green |
| Archetype | Self-mill graveyard combo, prepared engine, midrange shell |
| Size | 60 cards, 24 lands, 36 spells |
| Primary win | Squirming Emergence cheats a 5/5 out of the graveyard on turn three, then Abhorrent Oculus, Tolarian Terror and Balustrade Wurm close with evasion and trample |
| Secondary win | Hall of Echoes becomes a copy of the biggest creature on board for a lethal extra attacker |
| Land as engine | Hall of Echoes — {5} turns the land into a copy of a creature you control |

# Overview

The deck mills itself on purpose. Every cheap spell is a mill spell that also does something: Cache Grab
and Something Worth Saving both dig four cards deep and hand back a permanent, Primal Witchstalker mills
four and returns a land, and Theorix Metamage enters prepared so its Omit Variables can be cast once for a
free mill three. That fills the graveyard while keeping the hand stocked.

Once the graveyard has substance, two cards convert it into a board. **Squirming Emergence** returns a
non-land permanent with mana value less than or equal to the number of permanent cards in the graveyard —
after two mill spells that ceiling is already four or five, which is exactly where Abhorrent Oculus
(mv 3, 5/5 flier) and Balustrade Wurm (mv 5, 5/5 trample haste) live. **Abhorrent Oculus** itself is a
three-mana 5/5 flier that only asks you to exile six cards you were throwing away anyway, and it keeps
generating bodies with manifest dread on every opponent's upkeep.

The payoff structure is deliberately redundant: the deck can win from the graveyard, from the hand, or
from the land drop. Nothing in the list depends on a single card surviving.

# Approach

## Game plan phases

| Phase | Turns | What you are doing |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | 1–2 | Land, then a mill spell. Cache Grab is the default; hold Something Worth Saving if you already have a second copy in hand |
| Conversion | 3–4 | Squirming Emergence for an Oculus or Wurm, or just cast Oculus off six exiled cards |
| Consolidation | 5–6 | Rise of the Deathbringer either sweeps a small board or draws five off a 5/5; Hall of Echoes starts copying |
| Close | 6+ | Two 5/5 fliers, trample, and a copied attacker per turn |

## Card roles

| Role | Cards | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Self-mill engine | Cache Grab, Something Worth Saving, Primal Witchstalker, Theorix Metamage | 12 | Each is card-neutral or better; Witchstalker ramps a land back |
| Prepared engine | Theorix Metamage // Omit Variables | 2 | Enters prepared, so the mill three is free once; threshold turns it into a 3/4 flier |
| Reanimation | Squirming Emergence | 4 | The deck's turn-three play; permanent count is the ceiling |
| Fatties | Abhorrent Oculus, Balustrade Wurm, Tolarian Terror | 10 | 5/5s at 3, 5 and a heavily discounted 7 |
| Recursion | Balustrade Wurm (delirium), Gallia, Tragic Host (exile a creature card) | 4 | Both come back on their own; Gallia returns with a +1/+1 counter |
| Interaction | Bitter Triumph, Rise of the Deathbringer | 6 | Bitter Triumph answers anything; Rise is a -3/-3 sweep or a five-card refill |
| Selection | Stock Up | 2 | Looks at five, keeps two; the cheapest way to find Squirming Emergence |
| Bodies | Bestial Incursion | 2 | 4/4 trampler now, another one later from flashback |

## Lands as engines

| Land | Count | What it does for the deck |
|---|---|---|
| Hall of Echoes | 2 | {5}: becomes a copy of target creature you control, and the legend rule is switched off for the turn. Copy Balustrade Wurm for a second hasty trampler, or copy Oculus to double the manifest engine |
| Shipwreck Marsh | 2 | Untapped blue-black once you have two other lands |
| Overgrown Farmland | 2 | Untapped black-green on the same condition |
| Dreamroot Cascade | 2 | Green-blue, untapped from turn three onward |
| Forest / Island / Swamp | 16 | Green is the primary (12 green cards), blue and black are close behind |

The three duals are the "two or more other lands" cycle on purpose: this deck owns no planeswalkers, so
the Annex and Commons cycle would enter tapped every single game. Swapping them out was the last
correction of the build.

## Curve and mana

| Mana value | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cards | 0 | 14 | 10 | 2 | 6 | 2 |

Twenty-four lands with fourteen two-drops: the deck keeps one-land hands far more often than it keeps
zero-one-drops hands, and P(four lands by turn four) sits at 0.63. Tolarian Terror is listed at seven but
usually costs two or three after a couple of mill spells. Average mana value is 2.8, which is why the deck
can afford four Rise of the Deathbringer at five.

# Gameplay strategy

## Early game

Lead on a mill spell, not on a body. Cache Grab into Cache Grab is a fine opening because it puts eight
cards in the graveyard and returns two permanents to hand. Against fast creature decks, spend Bitter
Triumph early and accept the three life; the deck has no other way to interact before turn four.

Do not cast Squirming Emergence on turn three into an empty graveyard. It needs the permanent count, so
sequence mill first, Emergence second — by then the ceiling is usually four.

## The combo turn

The deck's "combo" is a two-card conversion, not an infinite loop:

1. Graveyard holds four or more permanent cards (two mill spells does it).
2. Squirming Emergence returns Abhorrent Oculus or Balustrade Wurm directly to the battlefield.
3. Oculus immediately starts manifesting dread on the opponent's upkeep; Wurm attacks the turn it lands
   because it has haste.
4. Rise of the Deathbringer then converts the resulting board into cards — draw equal to the greatest
   power, so five off a 5/5, at instant speed.

A resolved Oculus plus a second mill spell is usually enough: 5/5 fliers end games in this format, and
each manifest dread either adds a 2/2 or bins another card for the next Emergence.

## Win condition 2 — Hall of Echoes

Hall of Echoes is a real win condition, not a utility land. For {5} it becomes a copy of the best creature
you control until end of turn, and the legend rule does not apply that turn.

- Copy Balustrade Wurm: a second 5/5 with trample and haste, immediately.
- Copy Abhorrent Oculus: a second 5/5 flier, which also means a second manifest trigger.
- Copy Gallia, Tragic Host: a second menace body for the last few points.

Because the copy is a land until end of turn, it also survives sorcery-speed sweepers aimed at creatures.

## Mulligan guide

| Hand | Keep? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Two lands, one mill spell, one three-drop | Yes | The deck functions on three lands for two turns |
| One land, Cache Grab | Yes on the play only | Cache Grab digs for land two |
| Five lands, no mill | No | Nothing to do until turn five |
| Oculus plus Squirming Emergence, no mill | No | Both need a stocked graveyard |
| Hall of Echoes, three lands, two mill spells | Yes | The land is the finisher here |

## Key interactions and edge cases

- **Abhorrent Oculus' additional cost** is paid on cast, so a countered Oculus still costs you six cards.
  Only cast it when the graveyard is expendable — after Squirming Emergence has already taken what it needs.
- **Squirming Emergence counts permanent cards**, not total cards. Instants and sorceries in the graveyard
  do not raise the ceiling, but they do lower Tolarian Terror's cost, so the two plans pull in the same
  direction.
- **Balustrade Wurm's delirium recursion** wants four card types in the graveyard. Mill spells plus lands
  plus creatures usually get there by turn five; the instant count (Bitter Triumph, Rise) supplies the fourth.
- **Theorix Metamage is only prepared once.** The mill three is a single free cast, not a repeatable engine;
  its real value afterwards is a 3/4 flier once threshold is on.
- **Gallia exiles a creature card** as part of her recursion cost, which can shrink Squirming Emergence's
  ceiling. Recursion and reanimation compete for the same resource — choose which one you are spending on.
- **Rise of the Deathbringer's first mode costs life** equal to cards drawn; at five cards off a 5/5 that is
  a real cost when you are below eight.

## Matchups

| Opponent | Plan |
|---|---|
| Aggro | Board first, mill second. Bitter Triumph on their best attacker, Rise of the Deathbringer as a -3/-3 sweep, then Oculus blocks everything |
| Control | Mill aggressively and keep a second threat in hand; the deck loses to a single sweeper only if it over-commits. Hall of Echoes is the answer to sorcery-speed removal |
| Midrange | Race with Oculus and Wurm; their removal is one-for-one against a deck that rebuilds from the graveyard |
| Combo | No countermagic, so the plan is speed: turn-three Emergence into a 5/5 flier plus Rise of the Deathbringer for reach |

# Iterations

| Round | Change | Metrics |
|---|---|---|
| v1 | First 60: full mill package with Verdant Kraken top end, Twinned Vision, Insidious Roots, Silence the Echo | sim 50.7, T4 0.621, P(4L) 0.617, synergy 71.6 |
| v1 → v2 | -2 Verdant Kraken, -2 Silence the Echo, -1 Darklight Phoenix, -2 Twinned Vision, -2 Insidious Roots; +2 Rise of the Deathbringer, +2 Gallia, Tragic Host, +2 Stock Up, +1 Danitha, Spear of Agony | sim 50.7 → 51.7, T4 0.621 → 0.645, P(4L) 0.617 → 0.647, synergy 71.6 → 72.4 |
| v2 → v3 | -1 Danitha, Spear of Agony, -1 Diresight; +1 Abhorrent Oculus, +1 Squirming Emergence (engine density); then -2 Theorix Annex, -2 Formidable Commons, -2 Transformative Commons, +2 Shipwreck Marsh, +2 Overgrown Farmland, +2 Dreamroot Cascade (the deck runs no planeswalkers, so the Annex/Commons cycle entered tapped every game) | sim 51.7 → 51.0 (reruns ranged 46.3–51.7), T4 0.632, P(4L) 0.625, synergy 71.5 |

The build stopped at three rounds. Simulation win rate is the one gate that never cleared with margin:
the same 60 cards measured between 46 and 52 across repeats, so the shell sits right on the 52 threshold
rather than safely above it. Every other gate (size, legality, rotation, synergy, goldfish consistency,
land drop probability) passed on every run.
